_why: #24, measured live 2026-09-08. The evidence gate scored a codex leg `tools=0 ok=0 low-evidence (... possibly no reads)` while that pass filed three class-tagged must-fixes citing real seams. Its 522,203 B transcript held 1,554 tool references and exactly ONE brace-leading line out of 6,935 — enough for the old `any line starts with {` test to call it `parsed` and drop it to the delivery floor. Since #13 the gate DECIDES in one direction (a pass at or below the floor cannot certify a clean), and `hmad-surface-disagreement-second-mechanism.md` measures codex as the surface carrying 25 of 27 disagreements — so the misfire lands on the strongest surface, and only on its CLEAN verdicts. Each row restores one way this returns a confident zero where a cannot-judge belongs.

mutations.name: one-brace-line-makes-a-text-log-parsed-again
mutations._mechanism: Restores the exact defect. `agy_events` is ignored and a single JSON-ish line anywhere in a plain-text codex transcript scores it `parsed`, after which `ok=0` trips the delivery floor and the render says 'possibly no reads' about a pass that read 1,554 times.
mutations.replace:
if any(l.lstrip().startswith("{") for l in text.splitlines()):
        counts["shape"] = "parsed"

mutations.name: a-codex-log-is-scored-against-the-delivery-floor
mutations._mechanism: The shape is identified correctly and then ignored at the decision, so the codex leg falls through to `ok <= DELIVERY_FLOOR` and a clean codex verdict becomes UNVERIFIED on a measurement that was never made. This is the half that actually gates.

mutations.name: the-render-prints-tools-zero-for-an-unmeasured-log
mutations._mechanism: The verdict is right and the OUTPUT still says `tools=0 ok=0`. A reader takes that as a measurement — it is the number that started this whole finding — and concludes the pass read nothing. A figure this parser did not compute must not be printed as if it had.

mutations.name: absence-of-agy-events-is-taken-as-proof-of-codex
mutations._mechanism: The skip stops requiring the banner and fires on ANY non-agy log. A stray `--log`, a wrapper's stdout or the wrong path then inherits the skip and escapes the evidence check entirely — trading a false low-evidence for a false PASS, which is the worse direction. Positive identification is the whole point: absence of agy events is not evidence that a log is a codex transcript.

mutations.name: the-banner-is-matched-anywhere-in-the-file
mutations._mechanism: Dropping the head-of-file bound lets a transcript that merely QUOTES the codex banner — an audit report discussing a codex run, a pasted log excerpt — be classified as a codex transcript and skip the evidence check. Same substring-versus-anchor class as the allowlist row in the delta-review spec.

mutations.name: a-hollow-agy-leg-stops-being-scored
mutations._mechanism: The inverse direction, and it needs its own row because every other mutation here loosens toward NOT scoring. If the agy path also stopped being scored, a genuinely hollow agy leg — the case #13 built this gate for — would certify a clean again.
